title: Three issues, one archival route
publication: The Morgan City Daily Review (Morgan City, Louisiana)
purpose: An exercise in designing a documentary narrative from three issues of one newspaper. The corpus does not represent three independent institutional sources.
rights: Links only. No full-page scan is republished. Check Library of Congress rights information and contributor notices before reuse.

materials.title: Reports on local measures and the recruitment of volunteers
materials.status: the 10 October page reports local measures and the search for volunteers.
materials.use: First panel: initial public appeals for assistance
materials.not_demonstrated: The total number of relief operations actually carried out.

materials.title: Announcement about the local Red Cross committee
materials.status: the 11 October page reports on the local Red Cross committee.
materials.use: Second panel: organisation as reported by the newspaper
materials.not_demonstrated: The committee’s administrative results as established independently.

materials.title: More Nurses Needed / Shipyard Workers Organize for Relief
materials.status: the 14 October page carries two reports on relief efforts and a fund promoted by shipyard workers.
materials.use: Third panel: new appeals, a fund and anticipated cooperation
materials.not_demonstrated: Whether the collaboration took place or how many people received aid according to independent records.

curatorial_questions: What role does each issue play in the proposed chronology?
How would you cite the date, page, heading, digitising institution and provenance?
Why do three issues of one newspaper not provide three independent checks on the aid?
Which sentences need to attribute the information to the newspaper rather than present it as an established fact?
Which records from a different creator would help verify the interventions and their outcomes?

panel_proposal.title: The appeal
panel_proposal.label: The newspaper reported measures and a search for volunteers
panel_proposal.limitation: No independent account documents the activities announced.

panel_proposal.title: The committee
panel_proposal.label: The newspaper describes the formation of a committee and reported offers of help
panel_proposal.limitation: A news report cannot take the place of the organisation’s internal records.

panel_proposal.title: New needs
panel_proposal.label: Reports on the appeal for nurses and the shipyard workers’ fund appear on the same page
panel_proposal.limitation: Cooperation with the Red Cross is anticipated. Officials are the source for the account of aid provided.

panel_proposal.title: What is missing
panel_proposal.label: Administrative records and evidence of implementation still to be located
panel_proposal.limitation: Missing records prove neither the failure nor the success of the initiative.

review_points: The three issues are explicitly identified as coming from one newspaper.
Each panel retains a link to the date, page and original resource.
The panels distinguish reporting, intention and verified action.
Medical advice from 1918 is not presented as a current recommendation.
Images are reproduced only after rights have been checked.
limitations: The earlier comparison with the facsimiles does not constitute a new independent review.
This survey did not obtain records from other institutions confirming the extent or outcomes of the relief.
This exercise proposes a sequence of exhibition panels. It does not describe an exhibition already held.
student_product: A four-panel storyboard with an inventory of three newspaper items, seven captions or notes and a section on evidential limits.
